method: Clip duration, target runtime and frame rate are parsed as decimal values with at most three decimal places. Each duration is multiplied by the frame rate and rounded to the nearest whole frame, with values rounding below one frame rejected. Complete loops are the target frame count divided by the clip frame count and rounded down. The remainder is the final partial pass; total passes are complete loops plus one when a remainder exists. If the target is shorter than the clip, there are zero complete loops and one partial pass. If there is no remainder, the target ends exactly on a loop boundary and needs no partial pass. Displayed seconds and source out-points are derived from frame counts divided by the frame rate, so rounding remains explicit. Inputs are limited to 0.001-86,400 seconds and 1-240 fps. The tool assumes constant-frame-rate planning arithmetic and does not inspect media, model drop-frame timecode, create seamless transitions or render a video. It stores and transmits nothing.
